principle: Do not use the repository migration as a broad rewrite. Reduce accidental duplication only when behavior equivalence can be proved; schedule architectural consolidation behind stable adapters.

candidates.finding: Two progression models coexist: legacy Passport owns its own LEVELS/BADGES/streak logic while canonical progression owns generated levels, collections, rewards and discoveries. GameState carries both passport-derived progression and progression_engine.
candidates.risk: High: divergent rewards/levels, confusing migration semantics, duplicate source of truth.
candidates.action: FREEZE legacy passport semantics for M0; introduce explicit adapter/mapping; after behavior-equivalent migration, make canonical progression the only write authority and keep passport as projection/import compatibility.

candidates.finding: Legacy shoreline FINDS and generated collection registry coexist. The old module also owned direct legacy persistence before this refactor.
candidates.risk: High once Founding 141 arrives: duplicate discovery identity and reward paths.
candidates.action: This PR routes old finds storage through canonical adapter. Next: map the five shoreline finds to stable collectible IDs and make Progression/collection registry the only ownership ledger.

candidates.finding: Public origin/path is repeated as joaoccaldas.github.io/canyonmuseum across runtime, builders, schemas and generated/public files.
candidates.risk: High during repo/domain rename: partial rename can break updates, canonical URLs, RSS, schema IDs and SEO while appearing visually healthy.
candidates.action: Do not hand-replace generated output. Add one build-time SITE_ORIGIN/site metadata authority in a dedicated migration PR and regenerate all derived files.

candidates.finding: Native app name is KONA while Android appId remains com.caldasstudio.speedmaxmuseum.
candidates.risk: High before stable signing/public distribution because package identity is durable.
candidates.action: Dedicated native identity decision and migration before stable release signing; never bundle casually into repository M0.

candidates.finding: ~147.6k chars / ~1,950 lines. It coordinates scene construction, routing, interaction, persistence hooks and legacy hand-built rooms.
candidates.risk: High change blast radius and hard-to-attribute regressions.
candidates.action: No wholesale pre-migration rewrite. After M0, extract by seam: room construction -> navigation/walk -> interaction/cards -> lifecycle. Require identical browser evidence after each extraction.

candidates.finding: Data-driven wings coexist with hand-built hall/Sanctuary/pier/theme-room geometry.
candidates.risk: Medium-high: room metadata can disagree with rendered geometry and progression targets.
candidates.action: Keep stable room IDs/data registry now; port one room family at a time after migration. World registry should become authority, renderer becomes projection.

candidates.finding: Many consumer UI modules duplicated the same HTML escaping function despite a canonical esc helper already existing.
candidates.risk: Medium: security fixes can diverge across copies.
candidates.action: This stacked PR centralizes escape handling for core consumer UI modules and adds a source contract test. Keep companion-data escapeHTML as a semantic boundary for feed sanitization unless intentionally unified later.

candidates.finding: Avatar/User Studio surface is large and combines navigation, 3D stage lifecycle, drawer accessibility, avatar editing, sharing, races, feed/travel entry and settings.
candidates.risk: Medium-high: feature growth can turn it into the next landing.js.
candidates.action: Post-M0 split controller from views: studio-shell, avatar-editor, destinations, share drawer, stage loader. Preserve one User Studio route.

candidates.finding: Generated deploy bundles mirror source into several output surfaces. Deterministic checks exist, but duplicate files can be mistaken for source authority.
candidates.risk: Medium during migration and manual fixes.
candidates.action: Preserve current deterministic builders in M0. Add generated-file manifest/owner metadata and forbid manual generated edits. Do not reorganize outputs during repo copy.

candidates.finding: Token and component authorities are clear, but feature CSS remains large, especially race-self.css (~15.8k chars / 155 lines) and system-level rules can still overlap feature selectors.
candidates.risk: Medium visual drift; lower migration risk than state/runtime.
candidates.action: Do not compress CSS during M0. After migration run selector/property audit, move repeated controls/layout to components.css, leave feature geometry local.

candidates.finding: Older surfaces still carry local helper logic and Canyon-era language/state assumptions.
candidates.risk: Medium if mechanically renamed or merged into Kona.m shell.
candidates.action: Classify each as keep-as-exhibit, adapter, or retire. Do not automatically modernize every historical surface.

candidates.finding: Current operational docs, historical handovers and copied Canyon reference docs coexist.
candidates.risk: Medium human-error risk: stale docs can be treated as current truth.
candidates.action: At migration, move historical material under docs/archive or docs/reference-canyon and maintain one STATUS/PRODUCT/ROADMAP authority.

safe_pre_migration_normalizations: remove direct legacy persistence writes behind existing adapters
